acceptance_criteria.criterion: NavigateToRoot clears the entire stack and pushes the new root; CanGoBack is false immediately after.
GoBack when stack depth is 1 (at root) is a no-op — Current is unchanged and CanGoBack remains false.
GoBackTo(0) at root is a no-op; GoBackTo(n) where n >= stack depth - 1 is a no-op.
GoBack on a stack of depth 2 pops to the root; the root VM instance is the same object reference that was pushed originally.
NavigationChanged is fired exactly once per mutation call.
dotnet build produces zero errors and zero warnings.

summary: Implemented NavigationService.cs as a sealed class with a List<NavigationEntry> acting as a stack (index 0 = root, last index = current).
NavigateToRoot clears the list and pushes the new root, setting CanGoBack=false.
NavigateTo pushes an entry to the list.
GoBack is a no-op when Count <= 1 (at root); otherwise pops the last item.
GoBackTo is a no-op when stackIndex < 0 or >= Count-1; otherwise trims the list to the target index.
UpdateBreadcrumbs() rebuilds BreadcrumbItems as a BreadcrumbItem[] after every mutation, preserving StackIndex == list index.
NavigationChanged event fired exactly once at the end of each mutating method (NavigateToRoot, NavigateTo, GoBack, GoBackTo).
dotnet build --no-incremental produced zero errors and zero warnings across all 6 projects.
Updated docs/agents/project-manifest/file-tree.md and api-surface.md to reflect the new NavigationService class.

comments.note: NavigationService.cs: The _breadcrumbItems field is initialised to Array.Empty<BreadcrumbItem>() and always replaced with a new BreadcrumbItem[] after each mutation. If BreadcrumbItems is accessed from a UI binding while mutations are frequent, a single immutable ImmutableArray<BreadcrumbItem> could avoid repeated re-allocation, but at the current scope this is a negligible concern.

NavigationService.cs: GoBackTo with a negative stackIndex is treated as a no-op via the `stackIndex < 0` guard. No AC covers this case but the guard prevents potential ArgumentOutOfRangeException from List.RemoveRange, which is the correct defensive behaviour.

comments.note: NavigationService.cs: GoBackTo with an empty stack (Count=0) and stackIndex=0 correctly returns early because 0 >= Count-1 == -1 evaluates to true. This is safe but relies on the signed arithmetic of List.Count-1. No action needed — just worth noting as a non-obvious guard path.

[documentation-forward] INavigationService.cs: The interface has no XML doc comments. The GoBackTo(int stackIndex) signature is particularly non-obvious: stackIndex is inclusive (the entry at that index is kept; everything above it is removed). A summary comment on the interface method — and on GoBack, NavigateToRoot, and NavigateTo for completeness — would aid future contributors.

[documentation-forward] NavigationEntry.cs and BreadcrumbItem.cs: Both sealed records lack XML doc comments. BreadcrumbItem.StackIndex in particular (the list index used by GoBackTo) benefits from a one-line description to make the PageHeaderView wiring self-explanatory.
